chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Momineen (blessings of God upon him) used to strike with the hoe and cultivate the lands. And the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) used to suck the date pits with his mouth and then plant them, and they would sprout within the hour.
And indeed Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) freed one thousand owned slaves from his own wealth and the toil of his own hands.

key_terms.النَّوَى: Date pits/seeds — planting them was a common act of charity and cultivation
key_terms.الْمَرّ: A hoe or mattock, the primary agricultural digging implement of early Arabia
key_terms.كَدّ الْيَد: Toil of the hand — a classical expression for manual earnings, stressing the dignity of physical labor
key_terms.مَمْلُوك: A person in bondage; freeing (i'taq) a slave was among the highest acts of virtue

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do to earn money for freeing slaves according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates two accounts demonstrating the exemplary practice of manual labor by the Imams: Imam Ali (AS) digging and cultivating lands with a hoe, and Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) planting date pits that sprouted miraculously within the hour. The tradition further records that Imam Ali freed one thousand slaves from earnings of his own physical labor — illustrating that Islamic leadership demands personal engagement in honest work and that the fruits of one's livelihood must be earned through one's own hands before being devoted to charitable ends.
